Workloadsk8s 1.35

Job Parallelism and Completions

How does a Job run a batch of work to completion instead of serving forever? You give it completions, the number of successful runs you need, and parallelism, how many Pods may run at once, and it keeps launching Pods and retrying failures until that target is met. Once enough runs succeed it stops on its own and marks the batch complete. A failed Pod counts against backoffLimit, 6 by default, and exceeding that limit fails the Job instead.

▶ Play the animation 5 steps, animated, best on a wide screen

How it works, step by step

  1. A Job runs Pods until a fixed number of them succeed. This one asks for 5 successful runs and allows 3 at a time, so the controller sees 0 Pods running against a parallelism of 3 and creates 3 from one Pod template. Nothing has finished yet, so no completion is recorded and .status.active is 3.

    Play from this step

  2. Two runs finish cleanly: worker-1 and worker-2 exit 0. A Pod run that ends successfully counts once toward .spec.completions, so .status.succeeded moves from 0 to 2. A Pod that has succeeded is never restarted or reused, so the Job reaches the next completion by creating a new one.

    Play from this step

  3. The third run fails: worker-3 exits 1. Under restartPolicy Never a failing Pod reaches phase Failed, so .status.failed increments and no completion is recorded, and that failure counts against .spec.backoffLimit, 6 by default. The Pod object is kept rather than deleted, so its logs and its exit code stay readable.

    Play from this step

  4. Three completions are still owed and no Pod is running, so the controller creates 3 new Pods, which is the parallelism cap again. The replacement for the failed run waited out the back-off the controller applies to a recreated Pod, 10s then 20s then 40s and on, capped at six minutes.

    Play from this step

  5. The last three Pods exit 0 and .status.succeeded reaches 5, which equals .spec.completions. The controller stops creating Pods and records the condition Complete=True. The one earlier failure stays counted and the Job with its Pods waits for ttlSecondsAfterFinished.

    Play from this step
